Class Json

java.lang.Object
forj.json.Json
public final class Json extends Object
Encoding and decoding whole documents. The codec and the backend are givens: 
byte[] bytes = Json.encode(user);
User back = Json.decode(bytes);                       // A = User, from the typed local

import static forj.json.Json.*;                        // the same as extension methods
byte[] bytes = user.toJson();
User back = bytes.fromJson();

Decoding reads exactly one value and fails on anything but whitespace after it. A failure comes back in one of three ways, by method:

  • decode throws JsonException;
  • decodeEither returns it as Either.Left;
  • decodeF fails the effect: IO<User> u = Json.decodeF(bytes);.
